headline: Changes Chiricahua National Monument in Arizona into a national park and protects tribal access to cultural and religious sites there.
what_it_does: This law renames the Chiricahua National Monument in Arizona as the Chiricahua National Park. It directs the National Park Service to protect traditional cultural and religious sites in the park and to let members of Indian tribes use those sites for traditional practices. If a tribe asks, the Park Service may briefly close specific areas to the general public so tribal members can carry out these activities. Any closure must cover the smallest area possible for the shortest time needed.

who_it_affects.group: Members of Indian tribes with ties to the area
who_it_affects.how: They are guaranteed access to traditional cultural and religious sites in the park, and their tribes can ask for temporary closures to hold traditional activities.
Some specific areas of the park may be closed to the public for short periods when a tribe requests it for cultural or religious activities.
The agency must manage the site as a national park, protect cultural and religious sites, and handle tribal requests for temporary closures.

when_it_takes_effect: The law was enacted on October 20, 2026; the summary does not give a separate start date.
